title: PageRank by power iteration
experiment: Raising the damping factor d toward 1 slows power iteration, whose error shrinks by about a factor of d per step, which is why §3 can promise three decimals in fifty iterations at d = 0.85.
archetype_reason: PageRank is computed by repeating one update until it stops changing; one step is one iteration.

fixed.graph: 8 pages in two link cycles joined by one link; page 7 has no out-links

source.quote: follows a random out-link with probability d, the damping factor, and jumps to a random page otherwise. We usually set d to 0.85.
unless their rank is spread over all pages, rank leaks out of the web at every step.
The ranks are the fixed point of this update and do not depend on the starting vector.

metrics.name: residual
metrics.label: residual
metrics.meaning: L1 change of the rank vector in the last iteration

metrics.name: mass
metrics.label: rank mass
metrics.meaning: sum of all ranks; stays 1 unless rank leaks

reproduce.claim: At d = 0.85, fifty iterations bring the residual below 10⁻³.

source.quote: with d = 0.85 about fifty iterations reach three decimal places.

contrast.claim: At d = 0.99 the same fifty iterations leave the residual at least 100× larger, and above 10⁻⁴.

source.quote: As d approaches 1 convergence slows sharply.
